IS : 3888-1987 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

SPATULA, STAINLESS STEEL DENTAL 

( First Revision ) 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 



1. Scope — This standard specifies material, dimensions and other requirements for dental 
stainless steel spatula. 

2. Material — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 30CM3 of IS : 6603-1972 'Specifica- 
tion for stainless steel bars and flats'. 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 and 2.

All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 SPATULA, DENTAL 

3.1 The handle of the spatula may, however, be octagonal or round. 

3.2 Tolerances on various dimensions shall be in accordance with the following: 

a) ± 005 mm on dimensions up to 2-0 mm; 

b) ± 0'1 mm on dimensions above 20 mm and up to 5-0 mm; 

c) ± 0*2 mm on dimensions above 50 mm and up to 20'0 mm; 

d) ± 05 mm on dimensions above 200 mm and up to 50-0 mm; 

e) ± T'O mm on dimensions above 50*0 mm and up to 1000 mm; and 

f) ± 20 mm on dimensions above 100*0 mm. 

4. Heat Treatment — The spatula shall be uniformly hardened and tempered to a hardness of 
400 to 450 HV, when tested in accordance with IS : 1501 ( Part 1 )-1984 'Method for Vickers 
hardness test for metallic materials: Part 1 HV 5 to HV 100 ( second revision )'.

All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 2 SPATULA, DENTAL, ALTERNATE SHAPE 

5. Workmanship 

5.1 The spatula shall be made in one piece. 

5.2 The octagonal handle shall have cuts on all sides for the full length except space for marking 
on one side. The cuts shall be clear and clean. 

5.3 All the edges shall be even, free from pits and burrs, rounded and nowhere sharp. 

6. Surface Condition 

6*1 General — All surfaces shall be free from pores, crevices and grinding marks. The spatulas 
shall be supplied free from residual scale, acid, grease and grinding and polishing materials. 
Compliance with these requirements shall be checked by inspection using normal vision ( corrected, 
if necessary ). 

6.2 Surface Finish — The surface finish shall be one of, or a combination of, the following: 

a) Mirror polished; 

b) Reflection-reducing, for example, satin finish, matt black finish; and 

c) An applied surface coating, for example, for insulation purposes. 

Note — The satin finish should be effected by an appropriate procedure, such as grinding, brushing, 
electropolishing and, in addition, satin finishing (glass beading or satin brushing ). The finish should be 
uniform and smooth and it should reduce glare. 

Spatulas of mirror finish should be adequately ground to remove all surface imperfections and polished to 
remove grinding marks, resulting in a mirror finish. The mirror finish should be effected by an appropriate 
procedure, such as polishing, brushing, electropolishing, and mirror buffing. 

6.3 Passivation and Final Treatment — The spatulas shall be treated by a suitable passivation 
process, for example, by electropolishing or by treatment with 10 percent ( vjv) nitric acid solution 
for not less than 30 min at a temperature not less than 10°C and not exceeding 60°C. The 
instruments shall then be rinsed in water and dried in hot air. 

7. Tests 

7.1 Performance Test — The end of one of the blades shall be firmly applied to the surface of a 
porcelain slab and rubbed to and fro in a direction at right angles to the plane of the blade 
10 times. The test shall be repeated on the other blade. On completion of the test, the blades 
shall show no sign of damage. 



IS : 3888 - 1987 

7.2 Flexibility Test — The handle of the spatula shall be gripped in a vice in such a manner that 
about 120 mm of the spatula protrudes out of the vice jaws. By application of a force, to its tip, 
the blade shall be deflected by a distance of 6 mm in the direction of the application of the force 
and the force released thereafter. The test shall be repeated on the other blade. On completion 
of the test, the spatula shall show no sign of damage. 

7.3 Corrosion Resistance Test — The spatula shall be tested in accordance with IS : 7531-1975 
'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical instru- 
ments'. It shall show no sign of corrosion after the test. 

8. Marking and Packing 

8.1 The spatula shall be legibly and indelibly marked on the handle with the manufacturer's name, 
initials or recognized trade-mark; the words 'stainless steel' or letters 'ss'; and the country of 
manufacture. 

8.2 Each spatula shall be put in a polyethylene bag or wrapped in wax paper. The spatulas shall 
tnen ba packed in cartons in accordance with the current trade practice. 

8.2.1 Alternatively, the spatulas may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier. 

8.3 The packages shall be marked with the name of the instrument; number of spatulas in the 
package; the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; the words 'stainless steel*; 
and the country of manufacture. 

8.4 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

9. Sampling — Sampling procedure and acceptance criteria for the spatulas shall be as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier. A recommended scheme for the same is given in 
Appendix A. 



APPENDIX A 

( Clause 9 ) 

SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY FOR SPATULAS, DENTAL 

A-1. Lot — In any consignment, all the spatulas of the same shape, produced from the identical 
material under similar conditions and having the same surface finish shall constitute a lot. 

A-2. Scale of Sampling — The number of spatulas to be selected from each lot shall depend 
upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1 . 





TABLE 1 SCALE OF SAMPLING

A-2.1 These spatulas shall be selected from the lot at random and in order to ensure randomness 
of selection, procedures given in IS : 4905-1968 'Methods for random sampling' may be followed. 

A-3. Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity 

A-3.1 All the spatulas selected according to col 1 and 2 of Table 1 shall be examined for shape 
and dimensions, workmanship, and surface condition ( visual ). A spatula in the sample, failing 
to meet any of these requirements shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be considered 
as conforming to these requirements if no defective is found in the sample. 



IS: 3888 -1987 

A-3.2 The lot having been found satisfactory according to A-3.1 shall be further tested for other 
requirements. For this purpose, a sub-sample of size given in col 3 of Table 1 shall be taken. 
These spatulas in the sub-sample may be selected from those already examined according to A-3.1 . 
Each spatula in the sub-sample shall be subjected to hardness, performance, flexibility and 
corrosion resistance tests. The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of the 
specification if none of the spatulas in the sub-sample fails in any of these tests. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first issued in 1967. In this revision, the requirements for agate- tipped 
spatula have been excluded, tolerances on various dimensions have been specified, a recommen- 
ded scheme of sampling has been added and the clauses on surface condition have been modified 
besides incorporating certain other modifications. 

This standard does not include all types and sizes of the stainless steel spatulas, which are 
commercially available; it covers only those which are suitable for general purpose in dental 
surgery. 

The requirements for dental plastics spatula are covered in IS : 5541-1970 'Specification for 
spatula, plastics, clear and colourless, dental'.
